author: @whiskey_lima729
text:
Good morning ☕🦀🇺🇸

Pre-market overview – Friday, October 16, 2026 (~8:10–8:15 AM ET)

U.S. stock futures are mixed to slightly positive as markets catch their breath after a volatile week dominated by AI infrastructure concerns, higher yields, and inflation data. Dow futures are leading (roughly +0.3% to +0.4%), S&P 500 futures are modestly higher (+0.1% to +0.2%), and Nasdaq 100 futures are slightly lower (-0.1% to -0.2%).

Yesterday’s close (Thursday)
•Dow: +1.08% to ~52,178
•S&P 500: +0.33% to ~7,744
•Nasdaq: +0.08% to ~26,713

Indexes recovered from early tech weakness and snapped a three-day losing streak for the S&P and Nasdaq. For the week so far, the Nasdaq and S&P are on track for losses (Nasdaq roughly -2.4%, ending a four-week winning streak), while the Dow is higher.

Key drivers today
•Fed / rates: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s overnight comments in Bangkok did little to signal urgency for further rate hikes despite hotter-than-expected inflation readings earlier in the week. Markets are paring near-term hike bets. The 10-year Treasury yield is holding near ~5.08–5.11% after earlier spikes toward the mid-5.3% area.
•AI infrastructure pressure: CoreWeave $CRWV is down roughly 4.5–5% premarket (near $66–67) on ongoing concerns about its large debt load tied to GPU/data-center expansion. Broader neocloud and some chip names remain soft after this week’s selloff.
•Tesla $TSLA : Strong premarket gainer (roughly +3% to +5%) after Thursday’s long-delayed Roadster reveal at a SpaceX facility. The redesigned car (SpaceX thruster collaboration) demonstrated flying/flipping stunts, with claimed sub-1-second 0-60 and production targeted for 2028.
•Oil: WTI is hovering around $97–98 and Brent near $105–106, slightly softer on the day. Prices remain elevated on Middle East/Hormuz risks and U.S.-Iran tensions, but are being tempered by IEA emergency reserve releases and talk of possible easing around shadow-fleet restrictions. WTI jumped ~3% Thursday on a large U.S. inventory draw.

Other notes

Asian markets rebounded overnight (Nikkei stronger, Kospi recovering after a sharp prior drop). European indexes are mostly higher. Premarket movers also include acquisition-related strength (e.g., Varonis on a reported deal) and some earnings reaction (banks such as Travelers reporting).

Today’s calendar includes U.S. import/export prices, industrial production, and the Baker Hughes rig count, plus more bank earnings.

Overall tone is a cautious breather: rotation away from the most leveraged AI names is supporting the Dow and broader indexes, while tech remains fragile and oil/geopolitics stay in the background. Futures can shift quickly into the open.

author: @alphatrends
text:
ES and NQ are quiet this morning. Both markets remain below the declining 5 SMA and that means we still have a high level of defensiveness in our approach. 

The ES is right up against the WTD and MTD AVWAP, while NQ remains well below it. 

Keep a close eye on yesterday's vwap, the two day, today.  That is likely to be a place for buyers to defend it, could signal trouble if it fails to hold as support and gets trapped under it.  

As always, that is a scenario, not a prediction, there is a comfortable cushion down to the 2 day.  

We are waiting patiently for EVIDENCE buyers to gain control before we can trust rallies for more than a daytrade or small size.
